stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to obtain a prescription issued 13 months ago for a prescription-only drug that is not listed in Schedules I through V. The prescription record shows two authorized refills remaining. Which statements should the receiving pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The remaining refills keep the prescription transferable until both have been dispensed.
The drug falls within Massachusetts Schedule VI because it is a prescription drug not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V.
The transfer must be declined because a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance.
The transfer may proceed, but the receiving pharmacy must apply the federal six-month refill period for Schedule III through V prescriptions.
The rule allowing Schedule VI prescriptions to transfer in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions does not displace the separate one-year transfer ceiling.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts Schedule VI includes prescription drugs not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V. Although 247 CMR 9.14 directs Schedule VI prescriptions to be transferred in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions, it separately provides that a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance. Authorized refills do not extend that age ceiling, and the drug's Massachusetts Schedule VI status does not turn it into a federally controlled Schedule III through V drug.

choice_analysis.A: Authorized refills are relevant only while the prescription remains eligible for transfer; they do not override the one-year ceiling.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the facts place this prescription-only drug in Massachusetts Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: at 13 months, the transfer is outside the permitted one-year period.
choice_analysis.D: The Schedule III through V transfer mechanics do not make this Schedule VI drug federally controlled or substitute a federal refill period for the Massachusetts ceiling.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the general transfer-mechanics direction and the one-year Schedule VI limitation must be read together.

related_facts: A certified pharmacy technician may perform a Schedule VI transfer with approval of the pharmacist on duty
A Massachusetts pharmacy may not charge a fee for transferring a prescription
explanation.mpje_trap: The prescription has refills and follows Schedule III through V transfer mechanics, but neither fact erases the Schedule VI-specific one-year age limit.

reasoning_steps: Classify the prescription drug under the Massachusetts schedules
Separate the general transfer mechanics from the Schedule VI age ceiling
Measure the prescription age from issuance rather than from the last fill
Determine that remaining refills cannot cure an expired transfer window
